title: Ramp profile generator and conformance runbook for dedicated throughput
creator: Lena Cho
description: Deliver a repeatable, customer-facing throughput characterization flow for Dedicated capacity that combines: (1) a configurable ramp-profile generator (synthetic traffic) that mirrors realistic request-size and sequence-length distributions; (2) a conformance runbook that certifies throughput guarantees and verifies autoscaler behavior and fleet controls during upgrades/drain; and (3) a customer validation checklist and artifacts for sign-off.
motivation: Recent onboarding calls and internal postmortems show variability between synthetic stress tests and customer traffic shapes. Customers need deterministic proofs of throughput guarantees before Dedicated commits. This work reduces onboarding friction and aligns our SLA claims with measurable, repeatable tests.
success_criteria: A configurable generator that can produce four canonical profiles: ramp-and-sustain, spike-with-burst, sawtooth (periodic load), and long-tail steady-state
Conformance runbook with pass/fail thresholds for p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate, and tokens/sec that engineering + SRE can execute in <= 90 minutes
Automated data collection dashboard link (per-run) and an exported report template for sales/solutions to present to customers
Customer acceptance checklist that has been validated with at least two pilot customers and incorporated into onboarding materials
acceptance_criteria: Generator supports recipe files with: request-size distribution, sequence-length histogram, arrival-process (poisson, bursty, timed), and header-level variability
Runbook documents expected autoscaler signals and asserts (scale-up latency <= configured threshold, no cascading pod evictions), with remediation steps
Test harness integrates with tracing and per-token telemetry (KV-cache hit-rate, request-to-serve time, kernel saturation metrics)
Exports a single-run artifact (JSON) containing: run-params, raw samples, aggregated metrics, and deterministic seed used for traffic generation
tasks: Design ramp-profile DSL and implement parser (Lena)
Extend prober to model prefix/KV cache locality and token-length variance (Diego)
Add autoscaler observability hooks and synthetic node failure injector (SRE pairing)
Create conformance-runbook markdown with exact CLI commands and expected metric thresholds (PM review)
Wire up a per-run dashboard and a PDF/HTML report generator for customer sign-off
Run two pilot validations with real customer prompt sets and incorporate feedback
test_plan: Smoke: single-instance short ramp to confirm generator and collection pipeline (5m)
Stability: ramp-to-peak then sustain for 10 minutes, verify steady tokens/sec and p95 bounds
Autoscale exercise: repeated 30% step increases to trigger scale-up; monitor scale latency and node readiness
Drain & upgrade: orchestrate rolling upgrade during sustained load and assert no >2% error delta or >15% tail-latency degradation
Customer replay: run customer-supplied prompt set using recorded distribution and compare to baseline metrics
benchmarking_methodology: Warmup: discard first 120s of samples to allow caches and JIT paths to stabilize
Steady-state windows: measure three non-overlapping 5-minute windows after warmup to compute mean and confidence intervals
Significance: compute 95% bootstrap CI on tokens/sec and p95 latency; report non-overlapping CIs as meaningful differences
Determinism: each run must be seedable; record seed and environment (model binary, quantization profile, driver/kernel versions)
Noise controls: pin CPU governor, isolate NIC queues when possible, and run comparisons in the same fleet slice to avoid noisy neighbors
Failure injection: include controlled packet drops and simulated pod recycling to validate graceful degradation
runbook_steps: 1) Prepare environment: select tenant, model-version, and commit hash; snapshot config and KMS key IDs
2) Upload profile: provision recipe file into prober and verify parsing output
3) Warmup: run 2m warmup; confirm KV cache warming curve and GPU kernels initialized
4) Execute main sequence: run ramp profile, collect telemetry to prometheus/gcs, tag run-id
5) Monitor health: ensure node readiness, autoscaler metrics, and no >1% 5xx during ramp
6) Post-run aggregation: generate dashboard snapshot and export run artifact
7) Pass/Fail assessment: compare metrics to thresholds in this runbook; if fail, follow remediation checklist
8) Customer report: attach artifact and short narrative for engineering + sales sign-off
decisions: Use k6 for HTTP-level shaping and extend our prober to produce token-aware payloads (decision 2026-02-24)
Run steady-state windows of 5 minutes (trade-off between statistical confidence and customer time budget)
Report p99 and tail-99.9 in addition to p95 because customers care about worst-case SLAs
Keep generator recipes human-editable (YAML) rather than an opaque binary format to aid customer reviews
open_issues: Determine allowed variance for multi-tenant baseline (SRE input required)
Finalize which kernel/gpu metrics we surface in the customer report (privacy + IP concerns)
Decide whether to include synthetic model variants for graceful-fallback validation
blockers: Autoscaler API endpoint for 'recommended scale' is still under design (blocked on ENG-630001)
